images.title: Two thirds, four sixths
images.purpose: Show that 2/3 and 4/6 of the same ribbon are exactly the same length, which is why they are equivalent.
images.composition: Two flat ribbons of the same length, one above the other, with a small pair of brackets under the lower ribbon and a comparison line below.
images.exact_structure: Upper ribbon: a plain flat band cut into 3 equal parts, the left 2 parts filled teal #0072B2. Lower ribbon: exactly the same length, left edges lined up, cut into 6 equal parts, the left 4 parts filled amber #E69F00. The end of the teal length lines up exactly with the end of the fourth amber part. Under the lower ribbon, 2 small grey #6B7280 brackets, each spanning 2 amber parts, one under each teal third. Below, centred, one comparison line. Exactly 2 ribbons, 2 brackets, 1 comparison line.

images.takeaway: 2/3 and 4/6 are equivalent because their lengths are exactly equal.
images.description: Two ribbons of the same length, one in thirds with 2 shaded teal, one in sixths with 4 shaded amber; brackets show each third is 2 sixths, and the shaded lengths end together.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say why the lengths match: each teal third sits over exactly 2 amber sixths.

image_decisions.why: The reason 2/3 equals 4/6 is that the lengths match; one image of two ribbons shows it.
